sentences.en: And actually, the fact they've lost so many men actually emboldens them, makes their resistance more dogged.
sentences.zh: 所以英国远征军到这时几乎被彻底摧毁，并被新兵所取代。

sentences.en: So the British expeditionary force has been almost completely destroyed by this point and replaced by new men.
sentences.zh: 德军和法军各损失了约五十万人，但他们不想停下来，因为他们认为如果那样做，

sentences.en: The Germans and the French have lost about half a million men each, but they don't want to stop, because they think if they did that,
sentences.zh: 就辜负了那些阵亡将士的牺牲。

sentences.en: it would dishonor the sacrifice of those men who have fallen.
sentences.zh: 这就是背景。

sentences.en: So that's the context.
sentences.zh: 让我们进入 1914 年 12 月的战壕。

sentences.en: Let's get into the trenches in December 1914.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我们要看看西线那段 20 英里长的战线，一侧由英军把守，另一侧由德军把守，

sentences.en: And specifically, we're going to be looking at the 20-mile stretch of the Western Front, which is held by the British on one side and the Germans on the other,
sentences.zh: 位于比利时伊普尔以南。

sentences.en: south of Ypres in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些战线上的士兵大多是新来的。

sentences.en: So the men in these lines are newcomers, by and large.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些战线上的士兵大多是新来的。

sentences.en: They are reservists, they're new recruits who've been rushed in to take the place of the forces that were originally destroyed in the first few months of the war.
sentences.zh: 他们是预备役军人，是新招募的士兵，被匆忙派来填补战争头几个月里损失的部队空缺。

sentences.en: And that's true of the Germans as well.
sentences.zh: 德国人那边也是如此。

sentences.en: So they have poured in kind of young, inexperienced men, often from Saxony and Bavaria, rather than from Prussia.
sentences.zh: 所以他们投入了大量年轻、缺乏经验的士兵，他们大多来自萨克森和巴伐利亚，而不是普鲁士。

sentences.en: The British always said, you know, the Prussians are the worSt.
sentences.zh: 英国人总是说，你知道的，普鲁士人是最糟糕的。

sentences.en: They're kind of dour and dogged and formidable.
sentences.zh: 他们那种人阴沉、顽固且令人畏惧。

sentences.en: Bullet-headed.
sentences.zh: 死脑筋。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Whereas the Saxons and the Bavarians were jollier.
sentences.zh: 而萨克森人和巴伐利亚人则更开朗一些。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you get the first reports of fraternization between the trenches.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始听到关于战壕间联谊的最初报道。

sentences.en: This is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: It may surprise some listeners.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让一些听众感到惊讶。

sentences.en: The fraternization actually begins well before Christmas.
sentences.zh: 联谊实际上在圣诞节前很久就开始了。

sentences.en: So it actually happens from early November or so, from the point at which they dig in.
sentences.zh: 它实际上从11月初左右就开始了，也就是他们开始挖战壕的时候。

sentences.en: And what would happen is there would be a sort of informal shouted arrangement, and possibly, you know, sort of agreed by two men and meeting in no man's land or something.
sentences.zh: 通常发生的情况是，双方会达成某种非正式的口头协议，可能由两名士兵商定，然后在无人区见面之类的。

sentences.en: You know, we'll have a pause at this particular point in the day so that we can both wash,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们会在这天特定的时间停火，这样我们双方都能洗漱，

sentences.en: or we can have our evening meals, or because there's loads of bodies piled up in no man's land
sentences.zh: 或者我们可以吃晚饭，或者因为无人区里堆满了尸体，

sentences.en: and we'd like to retrieve our mates and bury the dead, or because the weather is really terrible.
sentences.zh: 我们想找回战友并掩埋死者，又或者是因为天气实在太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, it's pouring and pouring with rain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，雨下个不停。

sentences.en: The trenches on both sides are flooded.
sentences.zh: 双方的战壕都被淹了。

sentences.en: And basically, someone shouts out, you know, should we have a break so that both of us can repair our trenches?
sentences.zh: 基本上，有人会喊话，问我们要不要休息一下，好让双方都能修补战壕？

sentences.en: Which might strike people as mad, but I mean, you know.
sentences.zh: 这在人们看来可能很疯狂，但我的意思是，你知道的。

sentences.en: Well, but maybe it doesn't if you are not a professional soldier.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但如果你不是职业军人，可能就不会这么觉得了。

sentences.en: And, you know, you've, you've been working in a shop or an office or something, and suddenly you find yourself in the winter, in mud, facing people you know really nothing about.
sentences.zh: 而且，你之前一直在商店或办公室工作，突然发现自己身处冬天的泥泞中，面对着一群你根本不了解的人。

sentences.en: Wouldn't that make it likelier that you might kind of try and reach out and have an accommodation?
sentences.zh: 这难道不会让你更有可能尝试去接触并达成某种妥协吗？

sentences.en: Because you're not a professional soldier.
sentences.zh: 因为你不是职业军人。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, just by this point, you are a professional soldier, but you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，到了这个阶段，你已经是职业军人了，但你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: You're not, you haven't been raised to it.
sentences.zh: 你不是，你并没有从小接受这种教育。

sentences.en: You haven't been trained to it over many years to fight.
sentences.zh: 你没有经过多年的战斗训练。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, it's worth stressing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这值得强调。

sentences.en: There is always fraternization in wars.
sentences.zh: 战争中一直都有联谊。

sentences.en: You know, this is not unheard of, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并非闻所未闻，对吧？

sentences.en: There have been lots of examples in wars before this.
sentences.zh: 在此之前的战争中有很多这样的例子。

sentences.en: Remember that in this case, the front lines are very close together.
sentences.zh: 记住，在这种情况下，前线靠得非常近。

sentences.en: I mean, you can shout from one line and the other line will hear you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以从一条战线喊话，另一条战线的人能听到。

sentences.en: And the fraternization generally starts with the Germans.
sentences.zh: 而且联谊通常是由德国人发起的。

sentences.en: They're shouting in English.
sentences.zh: 他们用英语喊话。

sentences.en: And the reason it works that way is because there had been a real trend before the First World War for young German men, almost like kind of Australians or something today,
sentences.zh: 之所以会这样，是因为在第一次世界大战之前，年轻德国人有一种真正的趋势，就像今天澳大利亚人那样，

sentences.en: to come and work in London for a little while to improve their English.
sentences.zh: 去伦敦工作一段时间来提高英语水平。

sentences.en: They work as waiters.
sentences.zh: 他们做服务员。

sentences.en: It's a kind of stereotype before the war, the German waiter in a London restaurant.
sentences.zh: 战前伦敦餐馆里的德国服务员是一种刻板印象。

sentences.en: Yeah, so just to focus in on another angle then about what might have fostered fraternization,
sentences.zh: 是的，那么为了探讨另一个可能促进联谊的角度，

sentences.en: is there a sense even now that there is still a degree of commonality between Britain and Germany?
sentences.zh: 即使在现在，是否仍有一种感觉，认为英国和德国之间仍存在某种共性？

sentences.en: Because certainly that's there before the war breaks out, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为在战争爆发前，这种共性肯定是存在的，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I guess this is likely to happen between British and Germans than, say, French and Germans.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，这在英国人和德国人之间发生的可能性，比在法国人和德国人之间要大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the reason it wouldn't happen between French and Germans is, of course, the war is being fought on French soil.
sentences.zh: 所以，之所以不会在法国人和德国人之间发生，当然是因为战争是在法国领土上进行的。

sentences.en: French losses have been much heavier.
sentences.zh: 法国的损失要惨重得多。

sentences.en: And for the French, this is existential, right?
sentences.zh: 对法国人来说，这是生死存亡的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: This is their homeland from which they're trying to drive the invader.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的家园，他们正试图将入侵者赶出去。

sentences.en: The British are fighting on what they regard as a sort of neutral venue.
sentences.zh: 英国人是在他们认为的某种中立场地作战。

sentences.en: It's in a way a match for them as it is for the Germans.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这对他们来说和对德国人来说是一场比赛。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, we talked about this in previous series.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，我们在之前的系列节目中谈到过这一点。

sentences.en: Before the First World War, there was so much stuff about the kind of fraternal links between England and Germany, you know, the Anglo-Saxon heritage, all of that.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战前，关于英德之间兄弟般联系的内容非常多，你知道，盎格鲁-撒克逊血统，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And of course, that ends up being erased by wartime propaganda.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些最终都被战时宣传抹去了。

sentences.en: But we're only a few months into the war.
sentences.zh: 但战争才进行了几个月。

sentences.en: So I think there's still a lot of sort of, well, not a lot, but there was still a slight element of fellow feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为仍然存在很多，嗯，不是很多，但仍然存在一丝同胞情谊。

sentences.en: And I mean, a very obvious symbol of that cultural influence of Germany on Britain is the Christmas tree, right, which had been brought over by various royals,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，德国对英国文化影响的一个非常明显的象征就是圣诞树，对吧，它是由几位皇室成员带来的，

sentences.en: but particularly by Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband.
sentences.zh: 特别是维多利亚女王的丈夫阿尔伯特亲王。

sentences.en: And so, you know, that is a very vivid symbol of this shared culture.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是这种共享文化的一个非常生动的象征。

sentences.en: I mean, football, we'll come to football.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，足球，我们一会儿会谈到足球。

sentences.en: The Germans have basically imported football from Britain.
sentences.zh: 德国人基本上是从英国引进了足球。

sentences.en: And some of these people who've been waiters in London are shouting out about football.
sentences.zh: 而其中一些在伦敦做过服务员的人正在大声谈论足球。

sentences.en: They're saying, who's top of the First Division?
sentences.zh: 他们问，谁在甲级联赛榜首？

sentences.en: How are, you know, Tottenham Hotspur getting on or whatever?
sentences.zh: 托特纳姆热刺队表现如何之类的？

sentences.en: Although at this point, football isn't the kind of obsession that it will become for Germans.
sentences.zh: 尽管在这一点上，足球还没有成为德国人后来那种痴迷的东西。

sentences.en: It's much bigger in Britain, isn't it, than in Germany?
sentences.zh: 它在英国比在德国要大得多，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, agreed.
sentences.zh: 是的，同意。

sentences.en: So there are sort of reports of informal fraternisation.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些关于非正式联谊的报道。

sentences.en: And actually, as Christmas approaches, some of the senior commanders are worried that this might get out of hand.
sentences.zh: 事实上，随着圣诞节临近，一些高级指挥官担心这可能会失控。

sentences.en: So we talked before about a guy called General Horace Smith Dorian, and he was this sort of very gallant, kind of swashbuckling British commander
sentences.zh: 所以我们之前谈到了一个叫霍勒斯·史密斯-多里安将军的人，他是一位非常勇敢、有点侠义精神的英国指挥官，

sentences.en: who actually, before the war, had shocked people at the public school officer training corps by saying there should never be a war in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他在战前曾让公立学校军官训练团的人感到震惊，因为他说欧洲永远不应该发生战争。

sentences.en: It will destroy civilisation.
sentences.zh: 这会摧毁文明。

sentences.en: You know, and everyone had thought, gosh, this guy's an absolute, you know, look at this pinko pacifist, kind of telling us that he doesn't agree with war and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每个人都想，天哪，这家伙绝对是个，你看这个左翼和平主义者，竟然告诉我们他不同意战争之类的。

sentences.en: Anyway, he's now ended up in command.
sentences.zh: 总之，他现在最终负责指挥了。

sentences.en: And he issues an order on the 5th of December, and he says, you know, it's very common,
sentences.zh: 他在12月5日发布了一道命令，他说，你知道，这很常见，

sentences.en: he says, when you're close to the enemy, for men to slide into a live-and-let-live theory of life.
sentences.zh: 他说，当你靠近敌人时，人们很容易滑向一种“活着并让别人活着”的生活哲学。

sentences.en: They can become too pally, they lose sight of what he calls the sole object of war, and sink into a military lethargy from which it's difficult to arouse them.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会变得太亲密，忘记了他所说的战争的唯一目的，并陷入一种难以唤醒的军事怠惰中。

sentences.en: And so, as a result, he says, however tempting and occasionally amusing they may be,
sentences.zh: 因此，他说，无论它们多么诱人，有时多么有趣，

sentences.en: friendly intercourse with the enemy, unofficial armistices, and the exchange of tobacco and other comforts are absolutely prohibited.
sentences.zh: 与敌人的友好往来、非官方停火以及交换烟草和其他慰问品是绝对禁止的。

sentences.en: However, I think those key words there are, however tempting and occasionally amusing they may be, because it shows that even the man at the top can see the appeal.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为其中的关键词是“无论它们多么诱人，有时多么有趣”，因为它表明即使是最高层的人也能看到其中的吸引力。

sentences.en: That actually, sometimes it's a moment of tremendous relief and escapism to shake hands with the opponent.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时与对手握手是一种巨大的解脱和逃避时刻。

sentences.en: Anyway, we approach Christmas Day.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们临近圣诞节了。

sentences.en: The weather has been dreadful, pouring with rain, and so the recent fighting has been very desultory.
sentences.zh: 天气一直很糟糕，大雨倾盆，所以最近的战斗非常零星。

sentences.en: And on both sides, British and German, people are thinking a lot about Christmas.
sentences.zh: 双方，英国和德国，人们都在想很多关于圣诞节的事情。

sentences.en: So in the British newspapers, there have been all these appeals for the public to send tobacco and sweets and chocolates and Christmas puddings even.
sentences.zh: 所以英国报纸上到处都是呼吁公众寄送烟草、糖果、巧克力，甚至圣诞布丁的请求。

sentences.en: I don't know how they'd cook them, but anyway, Christmas puddings, plum puddings to the front.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们怎么煮，但总之，圣诞布丁、李子布丁送到前线。

sentences.en: The royal family have organised the sending of 350,000 Princess Mary gift tins.
sentences.zh: 皇室组织寄送了35万个玛丽公主礼品罐。

sentences.en: So Henry Williamson, in that quotation, mentioned his Princess Mary stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利·威廉姆森在引用中提到了他的玛丽公主礼品。

sentences.en: So you'd basically get a tin, and it had Princess Mary's face on it.
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上会得到一个罐子，上面有玛丽公主的脸。

sentences.en: And inside, there was some chocolate and tobacco and cigarettes and stuff.
sentences.zh: 里面有一些巧克力、烟草、香烟之类的东西。

sentences.en: And you got a lovely Christmas message from George V.
sentences.zh: 你还收到了一份来自乔治五世的美好的圣诞祝福。

sentences.en: And that's great.
sentences.zh: 这很棒。

sentences.en: And it's also great because in 100 years' time, it will enable Sainsbury's to use that as a way of flogging their own groceries, won't it?
sentences.zh: 而且这也很棒，因为100年后，它将使塞恩斯伯里超市能够将其作为推销自己杂货的方式，不是吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So everyone's a winner.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都是赢家。

sentences.en: Because there's a huge thing with chocolate and tins in the Sainsbury's adverts.
sentences.zh: 因为塞恩斯伯里的广告里有关于巧克力和罐头的巨大内容。

sentences.en: Now that said, although they've got this inspiring message from George V, one of Britain's very
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，尽管他们收到了乔治五世这位英国最优秀的国王之一的鼓舞人心的信息，

sentences.en: finest kings, most of the men are pretty miserable because they've been sitting there in this rain.
sentences.zh: 大多数士兵还是非常痛苦，因为他们一直坐在雨里。

sentences.en: They're cold, they're muddy, all of this.
sentences.zh: 他们又冷又脏，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But the magic of Christmas, when they wake on Christmas Eve, something has changed.
sentences.zh: 但圣诞节的魔力，当他们在平安夜醒来时，一切都变了。

sentences.en: So the rain has stopped, there's been a hard frost overnight, and the ground is kind of dusted with ice and snow.
sentences.zh: 雨停了，一夜之间结了严霜，地面上覆盖着一层冰雪。

sentences.en: So rather like you see in the adverts and the Paul McGannas video and stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像你在广告和保罗·麦甘的视频里看到的那样。

sentences.en: Christmas Eve is as normal.
sentences.zh: 平安夜和往常一样。

sentences.en: There's this sort of slightly desultory fighting and firing on both sides, gunfire.
sentences.zh: 双方都有这种稍微零星的战斗和射击，枪声。

sentences.en: But late that afternoon, the firing starts to die down as normal.
sentences.zh: 但那天傍晚晚些时候，枪声像往常一样开始减弱。

sentences.en: And then the Germans do something unexpected.
sentences.zh: 然后德国人做了一些意想不到的事情。

sentences.en: So we mentioned the presents that the British have had from home, and the Germans have had presents too.
sentences.zh: 我们提到了英国人从家里收到的礼物，德国人也收到了礼物。

sentences.en: The Kaiser, our old friend the Kaiser, has sent them cigarettes and tobacco.
sentences.zh: 德皇，我们的老朋友德皇，给他们寄了香烟和烟草。

sentences.en: But he and his men have also sent them lots of little Christmas trees, hundreds of little
sentences.zh: 但他和他的士兵也给他们寄了很多小圣诞树，数百棵小

sentences.en: Christmas trees, all across the front.
sentences.zh: 圣诞树，遍布整个前线。

sentences.en: And as night falls, the Germans start putting up these Christmas trees on the kind of parapets of their trenches, and they light candles.
sentences.zh: 夜幕降临时，德国人开始在战壕的胸墙上竖起这些圣诞树，并点燃蜡烛。

sentences.en: Go on, Tom, I can see you're gearing up to say something sardonic about the German candle lighting.
sentences.zh: 继续，汤姆，我看得出你正准备对德国人的点蜡烛行为说些讽刺的话。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全没有。

sentences.en: Paul, I just wanted to mention at this point, a podcast by a mutual friend of ours, Jonathan
sentences.zh: 保罗，我只是想在这一点上提一下我们共同的朋友乔纳森·威尔逊和罗伯·德雷珀的播客。

sentences.en: Wilson, with Rob Draper.
sentences.zh: 它就是它。

sentences.en: It was what it was.
sentences.zh: 很棒的标题。

sentences.en: Great title.
sentences.zh: 是的，也许不是最好的，但他的关于足球历史的播客。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's maybe not the best, but his podcast about the history of football.
sentences.zh: 在其中，他们提到了一个顶级事实，那就是这些寄给各个团和地方的圣诞树，他们也寄给了U型潜艇。

sentences.en: And in that, they mention a top fact, which is that these Christmas trees that get sent out to all the various regiments and places, they also send them to U-boats.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了一场非常有趣的辩论，讨论究竟如何在U型潜艇上平衡一棵圣诞树。

sentences.en: And they had a very entertaining debate about how exactly you would balance a Christmas tree on a U-boat.
sentences.zh: 你怎么在U型潜艇上平衡一棵圣诞树？

sentences.en: How would you balance a Christmas tree on a U-boat?
sentences.zh: 也许你用蜡烛点亮了它，而在U型潜艇上被烧死的风险，那一点也不节日。

sentences.en: Maybe you've lit it with candles and the risk of burning to death in a U-boat, which would be not festive at all.
sentences.zh: 总之，我只是顺便提一下。

sentences.en: Anyway, I just mentioned that in passing.
sentences.zh: 而且，我还想说一下德国人的圣诞树和平安夜。

sentences.en: And also, I just wanted to say about Christmas trees and Christmas Eve for Germans.
sentences.zh: 德国人，像大陆上的大多数人一样，对圣诞节有一种奇怪的态度。

sentences.en: The Germans have, like most people on the continent, have a weird attitude to Christmas.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们实际上不在圣诞节那天庆祝，对吧？

sentences.en: Namely, they don't actually celebrate it on Christmas, do they?
sentences.zh: 主要的焦点是平安夜，这在我看来总是很疯狂。

sentences.en: The main focus is Christmas Eve, which always seems to me mad.
sentences.zh: 确实很疯狂。

sentences.en: It is mad.
sentences.zh: 我不同意这一点。

sentences.en: I don't agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是不对的，但大概英国人并不真正了解这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, it's wrong, but presumably the British are not really aware of this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会，他们会被圣诞树的突然出现吓一跳。

sentences.en: And so they would be, they'd be startled by this sudden appearance of Christmas trees.
sentences.zh: 他们确实被吓到了。

sentences.en: They are startled.
sentences.zh: 所以那天晚上8点半左右，你听到了关于唱颂歌的最初报道。

sentences.en: So that evening at about 8.30, you get the first reports of carol singing.
sentences.zh: 同样，这是圣诞树陈词滥调的一部分，但这是绝对真实的。

sentences.en: Again, this is part of the kind of cliche of the Christmas trees, but it's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 所以8点半，一名皇家爱尔兰步枪团军官向总部报告，德国人照亮了他们的战壕，正在唱歌，并祝我们圣诞快乐。

sentences.en: So at 8.30, a Royal Irish Rifles officer reports to headquarters, Germans have illuminated their trenches, are singing songs and are wishing us a happy Christmas.
sentences.zh: 双方正在交换问候，但仍然采取了一切军事预防措施。

sentences.en: Compliments are being exchanged, but are nevertheless taking all military precautions.
sentences.zh: 所以你听到更多的报道涌入，说德国人正在唱《平安夜》，英国人则以《最初的诺埃尔》回应。

sentences.en: So you get more reports flooding in that the Germans are singing Stille Nacht, Silent Night, and the British are replying with the first Noel.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些颂歌如此忧伤其实很能说明问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think it's actually quite revealing that these are such mournful carols, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们几乎就像缓慢的哀歌。

sentences.en: They're kind of like almost slow kind of laments.
sentences.zh: 非常感人，但你知道，你不会在第一次世界大战期间唱《听，天使报喜》。

sentences.en: Very moving, but you know, you're not going to be singing Heart the Herald Angels Sing.
sentences.zh: 你不会在第一次世界大战期间大声唱出那个。

sentences.en: You're not going to be belting that out in the middle of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 有一些关于圣诞树的优秀书籍，我稍后会提到，

sentences.en: And there's some excellent books about the Christmas trees, which I'll mention a little
sentences.zh: 但目前，历史学家西蒙·琼斯的一篇在线文章中有大量关于人们点蜡烛和唱颂歌的记录和引用。

sentences.en: bit later, but just for the time being, there are loads of accounts of people lighting candles
sentences.zh: 如果你谷歌搜索“圣诞休战”，你就会看到它。

sentences.en: and singing carols, loads of quotations, on an online article by the historian Simon Jones.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，毫无疑问是德国人带头，他们开始鼓励英国人走出战壕。

sentences.en: If you Google the Christmas truce, you'll see it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在谷歌上搜索“圣诞节休战”，你就能看到相关内容。

sentences.en: And you know, there's no doubt whatsoever that it's the Germans who take the lead and they start encouraging the British to come out of their trenches.
sentences.zh: 而且你要知道，毫无疑问是德国人率先采取了行动，他们开始鼓励英国人走出战壕。

sentences.en: I'll just give one quotation.
sentences.zh: 我只引用一段话。

sentences.en: It's a British soldier called Private Frederick Heath.
sentences.zh: 那是一位名叫弗雷德里克·希思（Frederick Heath）的一等兵，他是名英国士兵。

sentences.en: He wrote a letter home a few days later.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他写了一封家书。

sentences.en: And he said,
sentences.zh: 他在信中写道：

sentences.en: All down our line of trenches, there came to our ears a greeting unique in war.
sentences.zh: “在我们的战壕防线沿线，我们听到了一种战争中独一无二的问候。”

sentences.en: English soldier, English soldier, a Merry Christmas, a Merry Christmas.
sentences.zh: “英国士兵，英国士兵，圣诞快乐，圣诞快乐。”

sentences.en: They spoke just like that, the Germans.
sentences.zh: 德国人就是那样说的。

sentences.en: For some little time, we were cautious and did not even answer.
sentences.zh: 起初，我们很谨慎，甚至没有回应。

sentences.en: Officers fearing treachery ordered the men to be silent.
sentences.zh: 军官们担心有诈，命令士兵保持沉默。

sentences.en: But up and down our line, one heard the men answering that Christmas greeting from the enemy.
sentences.zh: 但我们的防线上下，还是能听到士兵们回应着来自敌人的圣诞问候。

sentences.en: How could we resist wishing each other a Merry Christmas, even though we might be at each other's throats immediately afterwards?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么能拒绝互祝圣诞快乐呢，哪怕我们可能在下一秒就拼个你死我活？

sentences.en: And so they spend the night singing to each other across no man's land.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们就这样隔着无人区，彻夜为对方歌唱。

sentences.en: As he puts it, a night made easier by songs from the German trenches, the pipings of piccolos, and from our broad lines, laughter and Christmas carols.
sentences.zh: 正如他所言，那是一个被德国战壕传来的歌声、短笛声，以及我们防线上传出的笑声和圣诞颂歌所点缀的夜晚。

sentences.en: A thought strikes me, which is that we discussed in the series we did earlier this year
sentences.zh: 我突然想到一件事，我们在今年早些时候的系列节目中讨论过

sentences.en: about the atrocities in Belgium and the sense that the Germans have put themselves beyond the pale, you know, the evil Han and all of that.
sentences.zh: 关于比利时的暴行，以及那种认为德国人已经丧尽天良的看法，你知道的，什么邪恶的汉人（Hun）之类的说法。

sentences.en: You didn't get that conclusion from me, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那个结论可不是我得出的。

sentences.en: No, I know.
sentences.zh: 不，我知道。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: But there is a sense on the home front, isn't there, that the Germans are just monstrous.
sentences.zh: 但国内确实有一种舆论，认为德国人简直是禽兽，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But clearly, there's not a sense of that at all here.
sentences.zh: 但显然，在这里完全没有那种感觉。

sentences.en: They're not thinking this might be a trap.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没想过这可能是一个陷阱。

sentences.en: No, I suppose not.
sentences.zh: 不，我想没有。

sentences.en: But is that not because they have been there for weeks?
sentences.zh: 但这难道不是因为他们已经在那里待了几周了吗？

sentences.en: They know that the Germans are men just like them, as they, of course, will discover even more the next day.
sentences.zh: 他们知道德国人也和他们一样是普通人，当然，第二天他们会对此有更深的体会。

sentences.en: But that's what's interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这正是最有趣的地方，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I would guess that the effect of propaganda in Britain, and indeed in Germany, is to make them think, well, are they men like us?
sentences.zh: 因为我猜，英国乃至德国的宣传效果，就是让他们去想：他们真的是和我们一样的人吗？

sentences.en: Are they not monsters out to destroy civilization?
sentences.zh: 他们难道不是一心要摧毁文明的怪物吗？

sentences.en: It seems clear that that hasn't entirely taken root, that propaganda war.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，那种宣传战并没有完全扎根。

sentences.en: As we will see later in this episode, there are more truces after this, but they dwindle and they disappear by 1916 and 17.
sentences.zh: 正如我们稍后将在本集中看到的，此后还有过几次停火，但到了1916年和1917年，这些停火就逐渐减少并消失了。

sentences.en: And I think the truth is that over time, people became brutalized.
sentences.zh: 我认为真相是，随着时间的推移，人们变得残暴了。

sentences.en: But at this point, they're not fully brutalized.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，他们还没有完全变得残暴。

sentences.en: So they still see their opponents as human beings like themselves and not as, you know, not simply as the enemy to kill or be killed by.
sentences.zh: 所以他们仍然把对手看作和自己一样的人，而不是，你知道的，不仅仅是那种你死我活的敌人。

sentences.en: I suppose also there is a lot of sport-based propaganda, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 我想，这其中也有很多基于体育精神的宣传，对吧？

sentences.en: Certainly in Britain.
sentences.zh: 在英国肯定是这样。

sentences.en: I don't know whether it's the same in Germany.
sentences.zh: 我不知道德国是不是也一样。

sentences.en: So, you know, you mentioned this is kind of the equivalent of half time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你提到这就像是中场休息一样。

sentences.en: Perhaps that's also the sense that, you know, you fight hard, but shake hands.
sentences.zh: 也许那种感觉就是：虽然比赛时拼得很凶，但赛后会握手言和。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's Christmas Eve.
sentences.zh: 这就是平安夜的情况。

sentences.en: What about Christmas Day?
sentences.zh: 那圣诞节当天呢？

sentences.en: Christmas Day, dawn's cold and foggy, but by mid-morning, the fog has cleared and it actually turns out to be a lovely kind of crisp winter's day.
sentences.zh: 圣诞节那天，黎明时分寒冷多雾，但到了上午，雾气散去，天气变得格外晴朗，是一个典型的清爽冬日。

sentences.en: It's not raining, crucially.
sentences.zh: 最关键的是，没下雨。

sentences.en: For a lot of people, the most striking thing is how quiet it is.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，最令人震惊的是当时有多安静。

sentences.en: You know, the guns have been roaring all this time.
sentences.zh: 要知道，炮火声已经轰鸣了这么久。

sentences.en: But on both sides, a lot of officers say, well, we won't fire on Christmas Day.
sentences.zh: 但双方的许多军官都说，好吧，我们在圣诞节那天不开火。

sentences.en: So they just stop.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就停火了。

sentences.en: And once one side stops, the other generally then stops as well.
sentences.zh: 一旦一方停火，另一方通常也会跟着停火。

sentences.en: And then tentatively at first, you know, they've been making a lot of arrangements over the night.
sentences.zh: 起初他们还很试探，毕竟他们前一天晚上已经做了很多约定。

sentences.en: Oh, we'll get out of the trench if you do tomorrow morning.
sentences.zh: “如果你明天早上出来，那我们也出战壕。”

sentences.en: And men start to do it.
sentences.zh: 于是士兵们开始行动了。

sentences.en: And when no one shoots them, other men start doing it.
sentences.zh: 当没人开枪时，其他人也开始跟着做。

sentences.en: And bit by bit, along probably about two-thirds of this stretch, so we're talking about over a kind of…
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，在这段防线大约三分之二的区域，也就是我们所说的……

sentences.en: 12 miles?
sentences.zh: 12英里？

sentences.en: Yeah, 12 to 15-mile stretch.
sentences.zh: 是的，大约12到15英里的防线。

sentences.en: People get out of the trenches and they venture into no man's land on both sides.
sentences.zh: 人们走出战壕，双方都冒险进入了无人区。

sentences.en: And when they get there, what do they do?
sentences.zh: 当他们到达那里时，他们做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, they have made arrangements often.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，他们通常已经做好了约定。

sentences.en: I'll give you a tin if you give me, you know, some tobacco or whatever.
sentences.zh: “如果你给我烟草或其他什么东西，我就给你一个罐头。”

sentences.en: So they exchange their buttons.
sentences.zh: 于是他们交换了纽扣。

sentences.en: They exchange souvenirs.
sentences.zh: 他们交换纪念品。

sentences.en: Actually, Henry Williamson used the word souvenirs, I think, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 其实亨利·威廉姆森（Henry Williamson）用了“纪念品”这个词，我想是吧？

sentences.en: They exchange buttons and badges.
sentences.zh: 他们交换纽扣和徽章。

sentences.en: Sometimes they exchange their caps.
sentences.zh: 有时他们还会交换帽子。

sentences.en: That seems reckless because you might be shot by your own side.
sentences.zh: 这看起来很鲁莽，因为你可能会被自己人开枪打死。

sentences.en: I mean, explaining to the sergeant major of that in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我是说，第二天早上还得向军士长解释。

sentences.en: Why you're dressed as a German.
sentences.zh: 为什么你打扮得像个德国人。

sentences.en: The Germans hand over cigars.
sentences.zh: 德国人递过来雪茄。

sentences.en: The British will give them jam or tin.
sentences.zh: 英国人则给他们果酱或罐头。

sentences.en: But, you know, they'll basically sort of…
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他们基本上就是……

sentences.en: There's a sort of barter system.
sentences.zh: 有一种以物易物的系统。

sentences.en: Or a bar of Sainsbury's chocolate.
sentences.zh: 或者是一块森宝利（Sainsbury's）的巧克力。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Sometimes they have lunch together.
sentences.zh: 有时他们还会一起吃午餐。

sentences.en: There's a lovely account of the Sixth Cheshire's who managed to catch a pig and they roasted it in no man's land and shared it with the Germans.
sentences.zh: 有一个关于柴郡团第六营（Sixth Cheshire's）的动人故事，他们设法抓到了一头猪，在无人区烤了它，并与德国人分享。

sentences.en: Where the hell did they get a pig from?
sentences.zh: 他们到底是从哪儿弄来的猪？

sentences.en: God knows.
sentences.zh: 天知道。

sentences.en: God knows.
sentences.zh: 天知道。

sentences.en: There's a guy called Bruce Bairn's father who's often quoted in accounts of the Christmas Cheshire's because he became a very popular newspaper cartoonist between the wars.
sentences.zh: 有个叫布鲁斯·拜恩斯法瑟（Bruce Bairnsfather）的人，在关于圣诞节柴郡团的记录中经常被引用，因为他在两次世界大战之间是一位非常受欢迎的报纸漫画家。

sentences.en: He says, I spotted a German officer, some sort of lieutenant, I should think, and being a bit of a collector, I intimated to him that I'd taken a fancy to some of his buttons.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我发现了一名德国军官，我想大概是个中尉，作为一个收藏爱好者，我向他暗示我看中了他的一些纽扣。”

sentences.en: I brought out my wire clippers and with a few deft snips, removed a couple of his buttons and put them in my pocket.
sentences.zh: “我拿出剪线钳，利索地剪下了他的几颗纽扣，放进了自己的口袋。”

sentences.en: I then gave him two of mine in exchange.
sentences.zh: “然后我给了他两颗我的纽扣作为交换。”

sentences.en: And then Bairn's father says of the truce, the last sight he had of it was one of his machine gunners who was a bit of an amateur hairdresser in civil life,
sentences.zh: 拜恩斯法瑟在谈到这次停火时说，他看到的最后一幕是他的一个机枪手，在平民生活中是个业余理发师，

sentences.en: cutting the unnaturally long hair of a docile Bosch who was patiently kneeling on the ground while the automatic clippers crept up the back of his neck.
sentences.zh: 正在为一个温顺的德国佬修剪长得离谱的头发，那德国佬耐心地跪在地上，而自动理发剪正顺着他的后颈往上推。

sentences.en: My sense of Germans in the First World War is not that they had mullets.
sentences.zh: 我对一战中德国人的印象可不是他们留着鲻鱼头。

sentences.en: That's an unexpected discovery.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个意想不到的发现。

sentences.en: Yeah, but he's been in the trenches all this time.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但他已经在战壕里待了这么久了。

sentences.en: The mad thing is this bloke's got a load of clippers.
sentences.zh: 最疯狂的是这家伙居然带着理发剪。

sentences.en: Now, some activities are a bit more mundane.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些活动就比较平凡了。

sentences.en: So actually, both sides spend a lot of the truce fixing up their trenches.
sentences.zh: 事实上，双方在停火期间都花了很多时间修缮战壕。

sentences.en: And they even share tools with each other to work on their trenches, which is very sweet.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至互相借用工具来修整战壕，这非常暖心。

sentences.en: Some activities are not so sweet and a bit more sinister.
sentences.zh: 有些活动就不那么暖心了，甚至有点阴险。

sentences.en: So Simon Jones, who already mentioned, he quotes a British officer who shared a cigar with a German sniper.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·琼斯（Simon Jones）之前提到过，他引用了一位英国军官的话，说他曾与一名德国狙击手分享雪茄。

sentences.en: And this sniper very foolishly said, you know, I'm the best shot in the German army.
sentences.zh: 那个狙击手非常愚蠢地说：“我是德国军队里枪法最好的。”

sentences.en: I've killed more men than most of my comrades put together.
sentences.zh: “我杀的人比我大多数战友加起来还要多。”

sentences.en: And this British officer said, okay.
sentences.zh: 于是这位英国军官说，好吧。

sentences.en: Rightio.
sentences.zh: 知道了。

sentences.en: And he noted down this bloke's position so that he could shoot him himself the next day.
sentences.zh: 他记下了这家伙的位置，以便第二天能亲手干掉他。

sentences.en: That's harsh.
sentences.zh: 那真是太狠了。

sentences.en: But actually, the most common thing they did was to bury the dead.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们做得最多的事是掩埋死者。

sentences.en: There were loads of accounts.
sentences.zh: 有很多相关的记录。

sentences.en: Actually, you get one from Henry Williamson.
sentences.zh: 其实亨利·威廉姆森也提到过。

sentences.en: Of these mass burials.
sentences.zh: 关于这些集体葬礼。

sentences.en: And so they'll bury them all together.
sentences.zh: 他们会把死者埋在一起。

sentences.en: The German officers and men will line up on one side of the grave.
sentences.zh: 德国军官和士兵会排在坟墓的一侧。

sentences.en: The British on the other.
sentences.zh: 英国人排在另一侧。

sentences.en: They sing psalMs.
sentences.zh: 他们唱着圣歌。

sentences.en: They read prayers in both languages and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 他们用两种语言诵读祈祷文等等。

sentences.en: I mean, none of this sounds that exciting, frankly.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这些听起来并不怎么令人兴奋。

sentences.en: There's an awful lot of just sort of loitering and hanging around with your hands in your pockets.
sentences.zh: 大部分时间里，人们只是在那儿闲逛，双手插兜。

sentences.en: But it's clear from people's accounts that men on both sides found this a really remarkable and memorable day.
sentences.zh: 但从人们的记录中可以清楚地看出，双方的士兵都觉得这是非常了不起且难忘的一天。

sentences.en: You know, all these letters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有的这些信件。

sentences.en: The most extraordinary Christmas day imaginable.
sentences.zh: “能想象到的最非凡的圣诞节。”

sentences.en: I wouldn't have missed that unique and weird Christmas day for anything.
sentences.zh: “我绝不会错过那个独特而怪异的圣诞节。”

sentences.en: This one from Captain Sir Edward Hulse.
sentences.zh: 这是爱德华·赫尔斯（Edward Hulse）上尉写的一封信。

sentences.en: He describes singing Auld Lang Syne, with which we all, English, Scots, Irish, Prussians, Württembergers joined in.
sentences.zh: 他描述了大家一起唱《友谊地久天长》（Auld Lang Syne），我们所有人，英国人、苏格兰人、爱尔兰人、普鲁士人、符腾堡人都加入了进来。

sentences.en: It was absolutely astounding.

sentences.zh: 但在进入休息时间前，还有一个问题，他们会谈论战争吗？

sentences.en: That they'd talk about what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们会谈论自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Or about the quality of their food or whatever.

sentences.en: And actually, the most striking account of them talking about the war, for me, is this guy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对我来说，关于他们谈论战争最深刻的记录来自这个人。

sentences.en: We began with Henry Williamson, 19 years old.
sentences.zh: 我们从19岁的亨利·威廉姆森开始说起。

sentences.zh: 他目睹了葬礼。

sentences.zh: 他被德国十字架上写的话所震撼，上面写着：

sentences.en: Für Vaterland und Freiheit, for fatherland and freedom.
sentences.zh: “Für Vaterland und Freiheit”，为了祖国和自由。

sentences.en: And he's really stunned by this.
sentences.zh: 他真的被惊呆了。

sentences.en: And I quote, freedom, how was this?
sentences.zh: 我引用他的话：“自由，怎么会这样？”

sentences.en: We were fighting for freedom.
sentences.zh: “我们是在为自由而战。”

sentences.en: Our cause was juSt.
sentences.zh: “我们的事业是正义的。”

sentences.en: We were defending Belgium's civilization.
sentences.zh: “我们是在捍卫比利时的文明。”

sentences.en: And he says to a German bloke standing next to him, who speaks English,
sentences.zh: 于是他问身边一个会说英语的德国人：

sentences.en: What's all this?
sentences.zh: “这到底是怎么回事？”

sentences.en: What are you, what are you, you're the baddies.
sentences.zh: “你们，你们，你们才是坏人。”

sentences.en: What are you thinking?
sentences.zh: “你们在想什么？”

sentences.en: And the German says to him, well, of course we're fighting for freedom.
sentences.zh: 那个德国人对他说：“嗯，我们当然是在为自由而战。”

sentences.en: Our cause is juSt.
sentences.zh: “我们的事业是正义的。”

sentences.en: We are ringed with enemies.
sentences.zh: “我们被敌人包围了。”

sentences.en: So war was thrust on us.
sentences.zh: “所以战争是强加给我们的。”

sentences.en: We are defending our parents, our homes, our German soil.
sentences.zh: “我们是在保卫我们的父母、我们的家园、我们的德国土地。”

sentences.en: And Williamson has what he calls a most shaking, staggering thought, that both sides thought they were fighting for the same cause.
sentences.zh: 威廉姆森产生了一个他称之为最震撼、最惊人的想法：双方都认为自己是在为同一个事业而战。

sentences.en: These fellows in grey were good fellows.
sentences.zh: 这些身着灰衣的家伙都是好样的。

sentences.en: They were strangely just men like ourselves.
sentences.zh: 他们和我们一样，奇怪地只是普通人。

sentences.en: Very philosophical.
sentences.zh: 非常有哲学意味。

sentences.en: And also, Dominic, I'm amazed that this hasn't turned out to be a myth.
sentences.zh: 还有，多米尼克，我很惊讶这件事竟然不是虚构的。

sentences.zh: 我本来完全指望你会揭穿它。

sentences.zh: 是啊，我不喜欢揭穿真相。

sentences.en: So there was a truce.
sentences.zh: 所以当时确实有停火。

sentences.en: But I suppose then the obvious question is, well, how does it come to an end?
sentences.zh: 但我猜接下来的显而易见的问题是，好吧，它是如何结束的呢？

sentences.en: And also that question that you mentioned at the start of this first half, why didn't they just stop fighting?
sentences.zh: 还有你在这半场开头提到的那个问题，为什么他们不干脆停止战斗呢？

sentences.en: You know, why did they, when Boxing Day came, start shooting each other again?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么当节礼日到来时，他们又开始互相射击了呢？

sentences.en: Why did the Crumps return?
sentences.zh: 为什么克朗普一家又回来了？

sentences.en: And I suppose the biggest question of all, what about the football?
sentences.zh: 我想最重要的问题是，足球比赛呢？

sentences.en: Did they play that?
sentences.zh: 他们踢球了吗？

sentences.en: And if so, did the Germans win on penalties?
sentences.zh: 如果踢了，德国人是通过点球大战赢的吗？

sentences.en: We will find out after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息过后我们再来揭晓。

sentences.zh: 圣诞节在薄雾中破晓，仿佛一份礼物般展现并馈赠于世。

sentences.zh: 为了哈里、雨果、赫尔曼、亨利、海因茨。

sentences.zh: 伴随着哨声、挥手、欢呼、呐喊和笑声。

sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐，汤米。

sentences.zh: 一个挥舞着杜松子酒的年轻柏林人，是第一个从战壕里爬出来的人。

sentences.zh: 一个什罗普郡的小伙子像押韵诗一样向他跑去。

sentences.en: Then it was up and over every man to shake the hand of a foe as a friend or slap his back like a brother would, exchanging gifts of biscuits, tea, McConaughey stew, tickler's jam,
sentences.zh: 随后每个人都起身越过战壕，像朋友一样握住敌人的手，或者像兄弟一样拍拍对方的背，交换饼干、茶、麦康纳希炖肉、提克勒果酱作为礼物，

sentences.en: for cognac sausages, cigars, beer, sauerkraut.
sentences.zh: 换取干邑香肠、雪茄、啤酒和酸菜。

sentences.en: Or chase six hares who jumped from a cabbage patch or find a ball and make of a battleground, a football pitch.
sentences.zh: 或者追逐六只从卷心菜地里跳出来的野兔，又或者找个球，把战场变成足球场。

sentences.en: So that was The Christmas Truce by William McGonagall.
sentences.zh: 这就是威廉·麦格纳戈尔的《圣诞停火》。

sentences.en: Oh, no, it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，不是。

sentences.zh: 它出版于2011年。

sentences.zh: 它还被发行成了绘本童书。

sentences.en: And Dominic, you've written perfectly captures the slightly maudlin sentimentality that now surrounds this story.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你写的内容完美捕捉到了现在围绕这个故事的那种略带伤感的感伤主义。

sentences.en: Oh, no.

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得整个故事有一种帕丁顿熊式的感伤色彩。

sentences.zh: 是的，确实有。

sentences.en: But I guess we'll maybe come on to that in a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 但我猜我们过几分钟可能会谈到这一点。

sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，士兵们把战场变成足球场这个想法。

sentences.zh: 所以这正是过去20年左右真正引起轰动的事情。

sentences.en: So we mentioned the Sainsbury's advert.
sentences.zh: 我们提到了森宝利的广告。

sentences.en: It's one of the most discussed adverts of the 21st century in Britain.
sentences.zh: 它是英国21世纪讨论度最高的广告之一。

sentences.en: If you Google it, there's loads of commentary about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你去谷歌搜索，会有大量的相关评论。

sentences.zh: 它目前在YouTube上有2600万次观看。

sentences.en: And I think if you ask people now, especially children, what happened at the Christmas truce, they will say they played football.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你现在问人们，尤其是孩子们，圣诞停火期间发生了什么，他们会说他们踢了足球。

sentences.en: Now, this has become one of the most, bizarrely, one of the most hotly debated kind of questions of the whole First World War, particularly online.
sentences.zh: 现在，这已经成为第一次世界大战中最令人费解、也是争论最激烈的问题之一，特别是在网上。

sentences.en: Yeah, because I've read so many different opposing opinions on this.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我读过很多关于这个问题的截然不同的观点。

sentences.en: Yes, mad.
sentences.zh: 没错，太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And especially on social media, on Twitter or something.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在社交媒体上，比如推特之类的。

sentences.en: People will be ripping into each other about this question.
sentences.zh: 人们会为了这个问题吵得不可开交。

sentences.en: So let's get into the moSt.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们深入探讨一下。

sentences.zh: 这是最著名的足球故事。

sentences.zh: 所以如果你谷歌搜索或者看随便哪篇报纸报道，你会看到肯定有一场比赛，至少有一场。

sentences.en: It was played between the 133rd Royal Saxon Regiment, Germans, and a team of Scottish soldiers.
sentences.zh: 那是德国第133皇家萨克森团和一支苏格兰士兵队之间进行的。

sentences.en: They played on frozen ground, caps for goalposts, and the result.
sentences.zh: 他们在冰冻的地面上比赛，用帽子做球门柱，结果是。

sentences.en: The result.
sentences.zh: 结果。

sentences.en: Tom, are you really scoffing?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你真的在嘲笑吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。

sentences.en: I was, you know, caps for goalposts.
sentences.zh: 我只是，你知道，用帽子做球门柱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Caps for goalposts, I know.
sentences.zh: 用帽子做球门柱，我知道。

sentences.zh: 结果是德国队以3比2获胜。

sentences.en: So here's the most famous account that's often quoted from the British side.
sentences.zh: 这是英方经常引用的最著名的说法。

sentences.zh: 我们提供了足球，并用担架做成了球门柱。

sentences.zh: 我们的随军牧师乔利牧师担任裁判。

sentences.en: They beat us 3-2.
sentences.zh: 他们以3比2击败了我们。

sentences.zh: 但牧师表现出了太多的基督慈悲。

sentences.zh: 他们的左边锋打进了制胜一球，但他越位了好几米，哨声一响他就承认了。

sentences.en: And we spectators were spread nearly too deep along the touchlines with loaded rifles slung on our shoulders.

sentences.zh: 他在20世纪60年代接受了关于此事的采访。

sentences.zh: 他在采访中描述了一些常规的事情。

sentences.zh: 我们交换了香烟、杜松子酒和巧克力。

sentences.zh: 我是说，有个叫迈克·达什的人，引用了一位年轻军官的话，东兰开夏团的理查兹中尉。

sentences.en: This boat, Lieutenant Richards, was absolutely appalled by the Christmas truce.
sentences.zh: 这个家伙，理查兹中尉，对圣诞停火感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And he was delighted when this firing started again.
sentences.zh: 当枪声再次响起时，他很高兴。

sentences.en: He said, you know, good old-fashioned sniping.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，老派的狙击战。

sentences.en: He said, great to see some good old-fashioned sniping.
sentences.zh: 他说，很高兴看到一些老派的狙击战。

sentences.en: Because he was really worried.
sentences.zh: 因为他真的很担心。

sentences.en: He thought, you know, my men will be killed when the Germans attack because they'll just be trying to shake hands and the Germans will bayonet them or something.
sentences.zh: 他想，你知道，当德国人进攻时，我的士兵会被杀，因为他们只会试图握手，而德国人会用刺刀刺死他们之类的。

sentences.en: So this is why, you know, the headquarters on both sides issue orders no more fraternization in the period between Christmas and New Year.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么双方总部在圣诞节和新年期间发布命令，禁止再有联欢。

sentences.en: People like General Smith Dorian, he'd been to the front lines on Boxing Day, and he said, come on, this is a bit slack.
sentences.zh: 像史密斯·多里安将军这样的人，他在节礼日去过前线，他说，得了吧，这太松懈了。

sentences.en: You know, we can't be doing all this because the war will start again, and, you know, we need to be in kind of fighting mood.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不能这样，因为战争会再次开始，我们需要保持战斗状态。

sentences.en: So that's the officers.
sentences.zh: 这就是军官们的想法。

sentences.en: What about the ordinary Tommies?
sentences.zh: 那普通的汤米士兵呢？

sentences.en: Now, most of the accounts that we have from ordinary Tommies come, as you've already mentioned, Tom, from years afterwards,
sentences.zh: 现在，我们从普通汤米士兵那里得到的绝大多数记述，正如你已经提到的，汤姆，都是多年以后才出现的，

sentences.en: from a point at which it was common to see the war as a tragic waste.
sentences.zh: 从一个将战争视为悲剧性浪费的时期来看。

sentences.en: But at the time, the letters and diaries show that most men still very sincerely believed in their cause and wanted to fight to the end.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，信件和日记显示，大多数人仍然非常真诚地相信他们的事业，并希望战斗到底。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, even Henry Williamson, who goes on to become a pacifiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，即使是后来成为和平主义者的亨利·威廉姆森。

sentences.en: I mean, you said he becomes a machine gunner, and he's still having a crack at people in 1919, which I think shows excess enthusiasm for the war.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你说他成了机枪手，而且在1919年还在攻击别人，我认为这显示了他对战争过度的热情。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，没错，没错。

sentences.en: So another British soldier wrote later, there was not an atom of hate on either side that day, and yet on our side, not for a moment,
sentences.zh: 所以另一位英国士兵后来写道，那天双方之间没有一丝仇恨，然而在我们这边，片刻也没有，

sentences.en: was the will to war and the will to beat them relaxed.
sentences.zh: 放松过战争的意志和击败他们的意志。

sentences.en: But that's very kind of sporting ideology, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这是一种非常体育竞技式的意识形态，不是吗？

sentences.en: You know, you shake hands, but then you go out and you play hard.
sentences.zh: 你知道，握手归握手，但之后你还是得走上战场拼个你死我活。

sentences.en: Well, here's a perfect sporting message for you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这儿有个完美的体育精神讯息给你。

sentences.en: George Ede of the Rifle Brigade, he wrote to his family about the truce, and he said, I made friends with a German artilleryman who spoke good English.
sentences.zh: 步枪旅的乔治·埃德曾写信给家人讲述休战的事，他说，我和一名英语说得很好的德国炮兵交了朋友。

sentences.en: And when we parted, he said, the German bloke said to me,
sentences.zh: 当我们分别时，他说，那个德国人对我说，

sentences.en: Today, we have peace.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们和平相处。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, you fight for your country.
sentences.zh: 明天，你为你的国家而战。

sentences.en: I fight for mine.
sentences.zh: 我为我的国家而战。

sentences.en: Good luck.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运。

sentences.en: Now, that's lovely, but it doesn't suggest to me that they want a war to stop.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很美好，但这并不能让我觉得他们想让战争停止。

sentences.en: It suggests that exactly as you say, it's like sportsmen in a rugby match at halftime, you know, smiling and shaking hands,
sentences.zh: 这正如你所说，就像橄榄球赛中场休息时的运动员，你知道，微笑着握手，

sentences.en: and I'm going to absolutely go for you in the second half.
sentences.zh: 然后下半场我绝对会全力以赴对付你。

sentences.en: And here is something actually that will surprise people about ordinary soldiers.
sentences.zh: 这里有一件关于普通士兵的事，可能会让人们感到惊讶。

sentences.en: There were quite a lot of ordinary soldiers who did not approve of the truce at all and refused to honor it.
sentences.zh: 有相当多的普通士兵根本不赞成这次休战，并拒绝遵守它。

sentences.en: So, the second Grenadier Guards, they had suffered heavy losses before Christmas when the Germans popped up from their trench and shouted, Merry Christmas.
sentences.zh: 所以，第二掷弹兵卫队在圣诞节前遭受了惨重损失，当时德国人从战壕里冒出来大喊：圣诞快乐。

sentences.en: The Grenadier Guards shot them.
sentences.zh: 掷弹兵卫队直接向他们开了枪。

sentences.en: That would make a brilliant Sainsbury's advert.
sentences.zh: 那会是个绝妙的塞恩斯伯里超市广告。

sentences.en: There are accounts of Germans coming across no man's land and the British just shooting them.
sentences.zh: 有记录显示，当德国人穿过无人区时，英国人直接向他们射击。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not unheard of.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并非闻所未闻。

sentences.en: There are accounts of British units after Christmas fighting among themselves, those who have honored the truce and those who have not.
sentences.zh: 有记录显示，圣诞节后英国部队内部发生了冲突，一方是遵守休战的，另一方则没有。

sentences.en: Because the guys who have not honored the truce say to the others, you are traitors, you are weak, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那些没有遵守休战的人对其他人说：你们是叛徒，你们软弱，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: What were you thinking of?
sentences.zh: 你们在想什么呢？

sentences.en: You know, my mate died on, you know, the 12th of December or something, and here are you shaking hands with the people who killed them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的伙伴在12月12日左右牺牲了，而你们竟然在和杀害他们的人握手。

sentences.en: And actually, very strikingly, remember this is happening, as we said, it's an away fixture in Belgium and France.
sentences.zh: 而且非常引人注目的是，记住正如我们所说，这发生在比利时和法国的客场比赛中。

sentences.en: Simon Jones gives the example of a Royal Welch Fusiliers unit.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·琼斯举了皇家威尔士燧发枪团的一个例子。

sentences.en: They'd spent Christmas Day drinking with the Germans.
sentences.zh: 他们圣诞节那天和德国人一起喝酒。

sentences.en: They were withdrawn from the line on Boxing Day, and as they marched back, French women lined the streets to spit at them, saying,
sentences.zh: 节礼日那天他们撤出了前线，当他们行军撤回时，法国妇女站在街边向他们吐口水，说道：

sentences.en: How dare you have a great laugh with the people who have invaded our territory and despoiled our towns?
sentences.zh: 你们怎么敢和入侵我们领土、蹂躏我们城镇的人谈笑风生？

sentences.en: Do we know, was there any fraternization between German and French soldiers?
sentences.zh: 我们知道德国士兵和法国士兵之间是否有过任何联谊吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all, really.
sentences.zh: 没有，完全没有。

sentences.en: I mean, not surprising.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: The French are fighting for their native land, you know, and they've lost far more men than the British have.
sentences.zh: 法国人是在为自己的国土而战，你知道，他们损失的人数远比英国人多。

sentences.en: Well, actually, we'll come to an example later in the war where there is a truce between France and Germany.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，我们稍后会讲到一个战争后期法国和德国之间达成休战的例子。

sentences.en: But that's jumping ahead a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但那是稍微超前了一点。

sentences.en: So how does it all end?
sentences.zh: 那么这一切是如何结束的呢？

sentences.en: The fighting restarts on Boxing Day in a very half-hearted fashion.
sentences.zh: 战斗在节礼日以一种非常敷衍的方式重新开始。

sentences.en: It's actually not because the men are reluctant, it's because the weather turns bad again, because the snow turns to sleet.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是因为士兵们不情愿，而是因为天气又变坏了，雪变成了雨夹雪。

sentences.en: There's flooding in the trenches.
sentences.zh: 战壕里到处是积水。

sentences.en: So that means there's not that much fighting until New Year, and then in the New Year, the weather improves and the fighting can begin in earneSt.
sentences.zh: 这意味着直到新年之前战斗都不多，到了新年，天气好转，战斗便正式开始了。

sentences.en: Now, by this point, news of the truce has gone around the world.
sentences.zh: 此时，休战的消息已经传遍了世界。

sentences.en: It was broken by the New York Times, tellingly, I think, a paper from a neutral country on the 31st of December.
sentences.zh: 我认为很有意义的是，这条消息是由中立国的《纽约时报》在12月31日披露的。

sentences.en: And then you get a series of reports, mainly in Britain, actually.
sentences.zh: 然后你看到了一系列报道，主要其实是在英国。

sentences.en: It's interesting that the reports really are predominantly in Britain.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这些报道确实主要集中在英国。

sentences.en: So there aren't any in Germany, really, or France?
sentences.zh: 所以德国或法国真的没有任何报道吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: There are some reports in Germany, none at all, really, in France.
sentences.zh: 德国有一些报道，法国则完全没有。

sentences.en: I think it's because in Britain, the stakes are not quite as high as they are.
sentences.zh: 我想这是因为在英国，赌注并没有那么高。

sentences.en: I mean, they're pretty high.
sentences.zh: 我是说，赌注其实相当高。

sentences.en: I mean, don't get me wrong, they're still high.
sentences.zh: 别误会我的意思，赌注依然很高。

sentences.en: But it's not quite as existential as it is for the French and the Germans.
sentences.zh: 但对于法国人和德国人来说，这并不像对英国人那样关乎生死存亡。

sentences.en: And actually, the interesting thing, so the Manchester Guardian then was, the voice of liberal opinion, says,
sentences.zh: 而且有趣的是，当时的《曼彻斯特卫报》作为自由派舆论的喉舌，说道，

sentences.en: in fact, most papers say, oh, wasn't it lovely they had a truce on Christmas Day?
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数报纸都说：噢，他们在圣诞节休战难道不美好吗？

sentences.en: Quite surprising that even in the middle of propaganda, people, they applaud it.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，即使在宣传攻势中，人们还是为之喝彩。

sentences.en: The Manchester Guardian, the simple and unexamined impulse of human souls drawn together in the face of a common and desperate plight.
sentences.zh: 《曼彻斯特卫报》写道：在共同而绝望的困境面前，人类灵魂被拉近的简单而未经审视的冲动。

sentences.en: And then the Guardian has this line in the editorial.
sentences.zh: 然后《卫报》在社论中写了这样一行字。

sentences.en: It says, what would an alien from outer space make of the fact that we could stop on Christmas Day and then start again?
sentences.zh: 它说：如果外星人看到我们能在圣诞节停战，然后又重新开战，他们会怎么想？

sentences.en: Why would we start the killing?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要开始杀戮？

sentences.en: And the Guardian says, we might reply with great reason that there was very much to be done yet.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》说：我们或许可以很有理由地回答，还有很多事情要做。

sentences.en: That Belgium must be freed from the hideous yoke that has been thrust upon her.
sentences.zh: 比利时必须从强加于她的丑陋枷锁中解放出来。

sentences.en: That Germany must be taught that culture cannot be carried by the sword.
sentences.zh: 德国必须被教导，文明不能靠武力来传播。

sentences.en: There's the answer.
sentences.zh: 答案就在这里。

sentences.en: There is so much at stake, as they see it, even in liberal opinion, that people want to restart the war.
sentences.zh: 正如他们所见，即使在自由派舆论中，利害关系也如此重大，以至于人们想要重启战争。

sentences.en: They're not doing it reluctantly.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是不情愿地这样做。

sentences.en: They're doing it because they believe in it.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是因为他们坚信这一点。

sentences.en: You see, this is the classic Sandbrook twist on our Christmas Day special.
sentences.zh: 你看，这就是我们圣诞特辑中经典的桑德布鲁克式转折。

sentences.en: Ah, thanks.
sentences.zh: 啊，谢谢。

sentences.en: So, by mid-January, the war's back on in earneSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，到了一月中旬，战争正式重新开始了。

sentences.en: We'll be coming to the story of the First World War in 1915 next summer, in the summer of 2026.
sentences.zh: 我们将在明年夏天，即2026年夏天，讲述1915年第一次世界大战的故事。

sentences.en: Worth saying, this isn't the last truce of the war.
sentences.zh: 值得一提的是，这并不是战争中最后一次休战。

sentences.en: There was an official truce at Gallipoli, uniquely in the whole course of the First World War, in May 1915, to enable both sides.
sentences.zh: 1915年5月，在加里波利曾有过一次官方休战，这在整个一战期间是独一无二的，目的是让双方……

sentences.en: Right, because that wouldn't have been a Christmas truce, would it?
sentences.zh: 对，因为那不是圣诞休战，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Australians and Turks to bury their dead.
sentences.zh: 让澳大利亚人和土耳其人掩埋他们的死者。

sentences.en: There were more small-scale truces at Christmas 1915.
sentences.zh: 1915年圣诞节还有一些小规模的休战。

sentences.en: And actually, Theo will be shocked to hear this, there was a truce between French and German troops in the Vosges, Christmas 1915.
sentences.zh: 事实上，西奥听到这个会很震惊，1915年圣诞节，法国和德国军队在孚日山脉也曾有过休战。

sentences.en: And that actually inspired a German soldier, Richard Sherman, to set up the first youth hostel association after the war, because he was so inspired.
sentences.zh: 那次休战实际上激励了一位德国士兵理查德·谢尔曼，他在战后创办了第一个青年旅舍协会，因为他深受启发。

sentences.en: He wasn't Sherman as in the tanks as well.
sentences.zh: 他不是那个谢尔曼坦克的谢尔曼吧。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: I mean, that'd be quite a double bill, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那会是相当精彩的双重组合，不是吗？

sentences.en: That would be a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 那会是个转折。

sentences.en: But by 1916, 1917, there are no truces.
sentences.zh: 但到了1916年、1917年，就再也没有休战了。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because the battles of the Somme and Verdun, you know, the massive bloodletting means it's pretty much impossible.
sentences.zh: 因为索姆河战役和凡尔登战役，你知道，那种大规模的流血意味着休战几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: And also, you couldn't play football on the battlefield of the Somme.
sentences.zh: 而且，你也没法在索姆河的战场上踢足球。

sentences.en: I mean, that would be a total mess.
sentences.zh: 那会是一团糟。

sentences.en: Well, people tried to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有人尝试过。

sentences.en: A bloke started when the first day of the Somme, there's a very famous story about a man kicking a ball and chasing after him, shot immediately.
sentences.zh: 在索姆河战役的第一天，有个家伙开始踢球并追着球跑，结果立刻被射杀了，这故事很有名。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's not a match.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但那不是比赛。

sentences.en: I mean, you can kick a ball, but you can't dribble.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以踢球，但你没法带球过人。

sentences.en: He wrote on the ball, the great European Cup tie final, and then he was shot dead.
sentences.zh: 他在球上写着：伟大的欧洲杯决赛，然后他就被枪杀了。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah, terrible.
sentences.zh: 是啊，太可怕了。

sentences.en: So what happened to the memory of the Christmas truce?
sentences.zh: 那么关于圣诞休战的记忆后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: Here's an interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 这里有一件有趣的事。

sentences.en: Everybody forgot about it.
sentences.zh: 大家都把它忘了。

sentences.en: It was completely eclipsed after the war by allied joy and German, you know, bitterness and victimhood and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 战后，它完全被盟军的喜悦以及德国人的苦涩、受害者心态等等所掩盖了。

sentences.en: And actually, the Christmas truce as we know it today is really a product of the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们今天所知的圣诞休战，其实是20世纪60年代的产物。

sentences.en: And specifically, the play, Oh, What a Lovely War, produced by Joan Littlewood and her theatre workshop.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是琼·利特尔伍德和她的戏剧工作室制作的戏剧《噢，多可爱的战争》。

sentences.en: In Britain.
sentences.zh: 在英国。

sentences.en: And so this is something that is only happening in Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是在英国发生的事情。

sentences.en: It's not happening in Germany, for say.
sentences.zh: 比如，在德国并没有发生。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the theatre workshop was this sort of massive, there were massive lefties and pacifists and whatnot in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 那个戏剧工作室在60年代初是一群激进的左翼分子、和平主义者等等。

sentences.en: And what they produced, Oh, What a Lovely War, the play and then the film at the end of the 60s, was an indictment of the First World War,
sentences.zh: 他们制作的《噢，多可爱的战争》，先是戏剧，后来在60年代末拍成了电影，是对第一次世界大战的控诉，

sentences.en: and particularly of the generals and the political establishment and the kind of social hierarchy that lay behind the war.
sentences.zh: 特别是对将军们、政治体制以及战争背后的那种社会等级制度的控诉。

sentences.en: And so the sequence in the film, it's a very moving and memorable sequence to the soundtrack of Silent Night.
sentences.zh: 电影里的那个片段，伴随着《平安夜》的配乐，是一个非常感人且令人难忘的片段。

sentences.en: The whole thing is designed to hammer home the madness of the Western Front.
sentences.zh: 整部作品旨在强调西线的疯狂。

sentences.en: And this is what turns the truce into a kind of symbol for what people see as the horror and the futility of war.
sentences.zh: 这正是将休战转化为人们眼中战争恐怖与徒劳的象征的原因。

sentences.en: So I mentioned at the beginning, there were some excellent books on this.
sentences.zh: 所以我开头提到了，关于这个主题有一些非常出色的书。

sentences.en: There was a book for the 70th anniversary by Malcolm Brown and Shirley Seaton in 1984.
sentences.zh: 1984年，马尔科姆·布朗和雪莉·西顿为70周年纪念出了一本书。

sentences.en: And then another excellent book by an American historian, Stanley Weintraub, in 2001.
sentences.zh: 然后是2001年美国历史学家斯坦利·温特劳布写的另一本优秀著作。

sentences.en: And then, you know, we heard Caroline Duffy's poem.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，我们听了卡罗琳·达菲的诗。

sentences.en: But the real peak of interest came in 2014 with the centenary.
sentences.zh: 但真正的兴趣高峰出现在2014年的百年纪念时。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: I think this actually is also a reflection of its context.
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上也反映了当时的背景。

sentences.en: You know, the Iraq War is just a few years old.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伊拉克战争才过去几年。

sentences.en: The war in Afghanistan is still going on.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗战争还在继续。

sentences.en: This is the point 2014 when there's lots of stuff in the British headlines about the physical and mental health of ex-servicemen, servicewomen.
sentences.zh: 2014年的时候，英国头条新闻里充斥着关于退伍军人身心健康的大量报道。

sentences.en: People are wearing help for heroes, wristbands and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 人们戴着“帮助英雄”的腕带等等。

sentences.en: So that sort of, when the First World War centenary rolled around, I think the idea of the horror and the pity and the futility of war was very much on people's minds.
sentences.zh: 所以当一战百年纪念到来时，我认为人们脑海中非常关注战争的恐怖、悲剧和徒劳。

sentences.en: And the truce was a brilliant symbol of that for people.
sentences.zh: 而休战对人们来说是一个绝佳的象征。

sentences.en: Do you think also that there's just a deep vein of sentimentality about football in the British national character?
sentences.zh: 你是否也认为英国国民性格中对足球有着一种深厚的情感？

sentences.en: I don't know whether it's as virulent in other countries.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这种情感在其他国家是否也同样强烈。

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能不会。

sentences.en: But here, I mean, there's nothing like memories of an old football star or something to bring tears, a manly tear to the eye.
sentences.zh: 但在我们这儿，我的意思是，没有什么比回忆一位老球星更能让人热泪盈眶的了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: If you ever go to a Remembrance Day match, you know, in November, early November, it's a Premier League game.
sentences.zh: 如果你去参加11月初的阵亡将士纪念日比赛，那是一场英超联赛。

sentences.en: You know, these days, there's quite a big palaver about, you know, soldiers marching out and maybe a band and the last post and all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在会有很大的排场，比如士兵列队行进，可能还有军乐队、吹奏《最后岗位》等等。

sentences.en: I don't remember that happening decades ago, but it's become kind of institutionalized now.
sentences.zh: 我不记得几十年前有这种情况，但现在这已经成为一种制度了。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, football took over the 2014 commemoration.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，足球接管了2014年的纪念活动。

sentences.en: So your friend Prince William and the then England manager Roy Hodgson unveiled a memorial, which was people shaking hands inside.
sentences.zh: 所以你的朋友威廉王子和当时的英格兰主教练罗伊·霍奇森揭幕了一座纪念碑，上面是人们在握手。

sentences.en: Surprise, surprise.
sentences.zh: 不出所料。

sentences.en: A football.
sentences.zh: 一个足球。

sentences.en: Roy Hodgson, very intelligent.
sentences.zh: 罗伊·霍奇森，非常聪明。

sentences.en: Positively erudite, Tom.
sentences.zh: 简直博学多才，汤姆。

sentences.en: Owl-like.
sentences.zh: 像猫头鹰一样睿智。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Surely he listens to the rest of his issues.
sentences.zh: 他肯定听了剩下的节目。

sentences.en: Oh, I'd love to think so.
sentences.zh: 噢，我真希望是这样。

sentences.en: In one of his eight languages.
sentences.zh: 用他那八种语言中的一种。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The great irony of all this is the men in the trenches would be amazed that the truce looms so large.
sentences.zh: 这一切最大的讽刺在于，战壕里的士兵如果知道休战变得如此重要，一定会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Because, as we've said, the war went on for them because they believed in it and they wanted to fight it.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们所说，战争对他们来说还在继续，因为他们坚信这一点，并且想要打赢它。

sentences.en: And that is a really hard thing, I think, for most people now to accept.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这对现在的大多数人来说，确实是一件很难接受的事情。

sentences.en: So I think we delude ourselves into thinking that the 1,565 days of war were the aberration and the truce better reflects human nature.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们是在自欺欺人，以为那1565天的战争是反常的，而休战才更好地反映了人性。

sentences.en: And that is the Dominic Sandbrook message to the nation and the world on Christmas Day.
sentences.zh: 这就是多米尼克·桑德布鲁克在圣诞节给全国和全世界带来的讯息。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 精彩。

sentences.en: Happy Christmas, everyone.
sentences.zh: 祝大家圣诞快乐。

sentences.en: However, Tom, however, it is Christmas.
sentences.zh: 然而，汤姆，然而，毕竟是圣诞节。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: The lesson of history is that your neighbours are plotting to kill and eat you.
sentences.zh: 历史的教训是，你的邻居们正密谋杀掉你并吃掉你。

sentences.en: But let's end on a positive Christmassy note.
sentences.zh: 但我们还是以积极的圣诞氛围来结束吧。

sentences.en: And I think you should take us out with some lovely poetry from Carol Ann Duffy's festive poem to inspire the nation.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你应该用卡罗尔·安·达菲那首鼓舞人心的节日诗歌来为我们收尾。

sentences.en: Yeah, so some festive poetry and then perhaps right at the end, a little bit of music.
sentences.zh: 没错，来点节日诗歌，最后再加一点音乐。

sentences.en: And all that marvellous festive day and night, they came and went.
sentences.zh: 在那美妙的节日昼夜，他们来来往往。

sentences.en: And the officers, the rank and file, their fallen comrades side by side beneath the makeshift crosses of midwinter graves,
sentences.zh: 军官们，士兵们，他们倒下的战友并肩躺在仲冬坟墓那简陋的十字架下，

sentences.en: beneath the shivering shy stars and the pinned moon and the yawn of history, the high, bright bullets which each man later only aimed at the sky.
sentences.zh: 在颤抖羞涩的星辰、静止的月亮和历史的叹息之下，那些高处明亮的子弹，后来每个人都只是向着天空射去。

sentences.en: But Dominic, let's leave the last words on this Christmas morning to Sir Paul McCartney.
sentences.zh: 不过多米尼克，在这个圣诞节的早晨，让我们把最后的话留给保罗·麦卡特尼爵士吧。

sentences.en: I light a candle to our love.
sentences.zh: 我为我们的爱点燃一支蜡烛。

sentences.en: In love, our problems disappear.
sentences.zh: 在爱中，我们的烦恼烟消云散。

sentences.en: But all in all, we soon discover that one and one is all we long to hear.
sentences.zh: 但总而言之，我们很快就会发现，一加一才是我们渴望听到的全部。

sentences.en: Happy Christmas.
sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐。

sentences.en: Happy Christmas, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家圣诞快乐。

sentences.en: Happy Christmas, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家圣诞快乐。
